title: Salman Khan Is Reportedly Becoming Karna — and Bollywood Just Got Its Most Ambitious Epic in Years
excerpt: After years of mass-action romps, Bhai is in advanced talks to play the Mahabharata's most tragic warrior in a two-part epic directed by Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra and backed by Farhan Akhtar's Excel Entertainment. The body transformation alone tells you how serious this is.
body:
Picture Salman Khan, the man who has spent two decades flexing through slow-motion shirt-rips and dancing past the laws of physics, sitting still in a narration room — and being silenced. Not by an action sequence, but by a script. By a character. According to a Bollywood Hungama scoop, that's exactly what happened when **Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra** walked **Salman Khan** through the story of **Karna**, the Mahabharata's golden-armoured, eternally wronged warrior. The superstar reportedly heard it and was, in the words of a source, "bowled over."

Let that land for a second. This is the casting that could redraw the map of what a Salman Khan film even is.

> "He has heard the script and was bowled over by the characteristics of his part. He will be playing one of the most popular characters from Indian History and will undergo a complete makeover of his body structure." — Source, to Bollywood Hungama

The project is being mounted by **Farhan Akhtar**'s **Excel Entertainment**, which would mark Salman's first-ever collaboration with the studio *and* with Mehra — the National Award-winning director behind *Rang De Basanti*, *Bhaag Milkha Bhaag* and *Delhi-6*. Reports describe it as a two-part historical envisioned on a genuinely lavish, pan-Indian scale. Mehra has reportedly been chasing this Karna epic for years, with screenplay and music work already in motion; the role was previously linked to Tamil superstar Suriya before the long road of delays.

Why Karna, and why now? Because it's the most cunning piece of casting in the room. Karna is the warrior who is great and good and utterly cheated by fate — abandoned at birth, mocked for his lineage, loyal to the wrong side, undone not by weakness but by a series of cruel curses. He is the character every Indian grandmother sighs over. For an actor whose off-screen image has weathered its own storms, there's something almost meta about Salman picking the man history refused to forgive. The "larger-than-life aura" that a source says drew him to the part isn't marketing fluff here — Karna *is* larger than life, and tragic with it. The casting practically writes its own emotional climax.

Then there's that line about the "complete makeover of his body structure." Salman transforming his physique is not, in itself, news. But a transformation *for a period warrior* — armour, scale, the weight of an era — is a different ask than another gym-sculpted action hero. It signals that everyone involved wants spectacle with gravitas, not just biceps in a dhoti. Think of the bar South Indian cinema has set with its mytho-epics; Bollywood has been visibly hungry to answer, and a Karna with Salman's box-office pull could be that answer.

Nothing is signed yet — let's be clear-eyed about that. A source told Bollywood Hungama that discussions with Excel are ongoing "on multiple fronts," especially shooting days and remuneration, and that Salman "needs his time before making an informed decision." If it all comes together, cameras are expected to roll by **Summer 2027**, right after he wraps the Raj & DK-directed superhero comedy that's also on his plate. Add the Apoorva Lakhia film *Matrubhoomi* and the Vamshi Paidipally-directed *SVC63* opposite Nayanthara, and the picture is of a star deliberately stacking big, varied swings rather than coasting.

## The diaspora angle

For NRI audiences across the **US, UK and Canada**, a Salman-led Mahabharata epic is the kind of event film that fills weekend multiplex shows in New Jersey, Toronto and Wembley — the sort of release that turns into a community outing. Mythological epics travel especially well in the diaspora, where parents want their kids to absorb the stories they grew up on, dressed in the production scale of a global blockbuster. Expect, if this materialises, a wide international theatrical rollout with Hindi plus dubbed Tamil and Telugu versions, and eventual streaming on a major platform.

For now, it remains a tantalising "if." But it's the kind of "if" that should have every film fan leaning in. Salman Khan as Karna, directed by the man who gave us *Bhaag Milkha Bhaag*, produced by Excel — on paper, that's not a movie. That's a moment. Here's hoping the dotted line gets signed.
